column1: # diff-side-addresses.tsv — THE confrontation table for how ONE side of a
# A comparison is a URL naming two SIDES, and a side is either a stored blob id
# (att- + 12 lowercase hex) or a document address
#                                  address; everything else reads what it says.
#   cli/ocagent/diff.go            a PRE-FLIGHT copy, so a mistyped side costs
#                                  one local sentence naming WHICH argument is
#                                  wrong instead of a round trip that cannot.
#                                  The plain (unsigned) flavour makes no request
#                                  at all, so without this copy that flavour
#   frontend/                      a READER of the contract: it parses the same
#                                  address out of the page URL to draw each
#                                  column. When it disagrees, the server wins.
# NONE of the three can be derived from another: the two Go copies live in
# separate modules with no import path between them, and the cockpit is a
# different language entirely. So each is confronted against THIS TABLE instead
# of against its neighbour, which is what makes a drift name the copy that
# drifted rather than merely reporting that two copies differ:
# All THREE copies are driven from this table. Add a row and every copy that
# disagrees with it goes red by name — which is the whole reason the cases live
# here as data rather than inside any one implementation's test code.
# WHAT "SAYABLE" MEANS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
# A row marked `ok` promises the address is SAYABLE — never that it resolves.
# Whether a blob is still stored or a revision still retained is a read-time
# fact, answered by that side's honest "this side is gone", not by a refusal.
# FORMAT (tab-separated; '#' comments and blank lines ignored)
#   address <TAB> ok|bad <TAB> what this row is about
# The literal token <space> stands for one space character. Padded addresses are
# the rows whose exactness matters most (they are refused, because the value is
# matched AS GIVEN and a padded address resolves to nothing), and a bare space
# between two tabs is too easy for an editor to eat.

column3: a stored blob id: att- plus exactly 12 lowercase hex
the same shape, different digits
the easiest typo of all — an id copied without its tail
eleven digits is not twelve
thirteen digits is not twelve
uppercase hex is not the shape the mint prints
'g' is not a hex digit
traversal: a reader that concatenates would fetch another endpoint
a leading space — matched as given, so it names nothing
a trailing space, for the same reason
no att- prefix
a file path: diff uploads nothing, upload it first
the live content of a document
the shipped default
a retained revision, addressed by its id
one field of a multi-field document
a kind whose field is not called text
SAYABLE but unresolvable: kinds are not enumerated here, and a kind this station lacks is a gone side at read time, not a refusal
three segments — the address is kind/key/at/field
five segments
an empty key
an empty field
an empty kind
'..' traverses without containing an excluded character
'.' likewise
'%' is excluded: a reader splicing this into a URL would re-decode it
'?' would end the path and start a query
'#' would end the URL
'latest' is not one of current, seed or a revision id
a revision id never starts at zero
a leading zero is not the decimal spelling of an id
a padded at — matched as given
a space inside a field name
the prefix alone names nothing
whitespace only
